sourceAssessment.identity: One-cell low restaurant wall, blue coping over horizontal honey timber, finished terminal at the right of S and only one open connection at W.
sourceAssessment.shapeVolume: The broad S/N faces read clearly as a wall, but the coping is a large nearly flat blue field and the post reads as a narrow vertical bar with an isolated bright top segment. E/W expose especially simple rectangular top/post shapes.
sourceAssessment.color: Blue and honey timber are already distinguishable. The blue is flat and saturated; lower timber and the terminal post descend into a heavy brown ramp instead of maintaining warm readable material volume.
sourceAssessment.lightingHighlights: Existing large surfaces have little broad curvature or edge response. The post top is bright, while the shaft/base lose useful form, particularly in W.
sourceAssessment.materialDetail: Horizontal divisions establish timber construction, but the flat faces and minimal finish do not yet express crafted wood and ceramic. The post lacks a coherent finished cap-to-shaft-to-ground construction.
sourceAssessment.intendedSizeReadability: At logical scale the source silhouette and palette are legible. Small existing strips compress into dark lines; the thin terminal is much less descriptive than the target design.
sourceAssessment.defectRisk: No candidate reviewed. Inspect every real rotation: the W-facing terminal shaft/base and E-facing open-profile view are important places to catch muddy shading, apparent hanging bars and coping/post overlaps.

usefulOutcomes: A terminal that looks deliberately constructed: a substantial shaft with a resolved top, coping junction and base rather than a dangling bar.
Soft, readable edge transitions and broad highlight planes that give the coping and timber solid cartoon volume.
Warm honey timber with controlled broad grain and distinct blue ceramic; detail survives small size without turning into noise.
A finish consistent with the family concept while retaining the end-cap role.
notLiteralRequirements: Original part counts, weak forms, exact board count and blank surfaces are not aesthetic constraints.
The imagegen reference does not prove camera, occupied scale, height, W continuity or unseen views. Its proportion changes cannot override the native contract.
Thin white highlight outlines, extreme gloss and isolated alpha specks/colored fringe from image generation should not be copied.
Cap, collar or foot details are useful examples of designed construction, not a mandatory recipe; equivalent native design is welcome within the envelope.
